name: kochi
title: Kochi, Kerala
note: Monsoon city on the backwaters. Chosen because KSDMA publishes depth-valued flood hazard rasters by return period, which is what the validated tier is checked against.

terrain.source: DeltaDTM v1.1 (Pronk et al. 2024), via Earth Engine community catalog
terrain.note: Raw band. Non-finite is sea or outside coverage; the value 30 is the model's cap.

official.source: Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA), produced with UNEP
official.title: Flood Hazard Probability of Kerala based on Historic Data
official.units: cm (inferred from magnitude; not stated at source)
official.licence: Published by KSDMA for public use; terms not stated on the download page
caveats: Displayed as published: clipped only, never resampled or reinterpreted.
Coarser than our screening grid (~92 m against 10 m), so it shows the floodplain, not which street corner fills.
Units are inferred from magnitude, not stated at source.
RCP8.5 climate-scenario rasters also exist and are not staged.

population.extent: Kochi urban agglomeration, 2011 Census of India
population.note: The staged box is greater Kochi and is not an exact match for the UA boundary, so the count is an order of magnitude, not a precise total.

news_query: (Kochi OR Ernakulam) Kerala (flood OR flooding OR waterlogging OR rain)

preparations.budget_line: Kochi Corporation seasonal preparedness line (about ₹5 crore), under Kerala SDRF 2026 budget rules

clear_outlet_drain.label: Clear / desilt the outlet drain or canal

barricade_low_stretch.label: Barricade and sign the low stretch

infeasible.label: Raise the road level
infeasible.reason: Capital work, outside the corporation's seasonal preparedness budget line

infeasible.label: Lay a new storm-drain network
infeasible.reason: Multi-year capital project, not a pre-season preparation

preparations.source: Kerala SDRF 2026 budget rules; Operation Breakthrough canal-desilting orders; Kochi Corporation and Ernakulam DDMA (documented figures, not a live feed)

bands.label: the temperature IMD requires at a coastal station

heat_standard.incomplete: At a coastal station IMD needs two things together: the day at or above the temperature named here, AND that day running well above the station's own long-run normal. No normal is staged for this city, so this product never declares a heat wave. It reports only whether the temperature half of the criterion is met, and says the other half is unchecked.

surface_heat.source: Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level 2 surface temperature (USGS), via Earth Engine
surface_heat.licence: USGS Landsat data are public domain
surface_heat.season: January to April, the dry months before the monsoon
surface_heat.composite: median of every clear view; cloud, cirrus, shadow and water masked
surface_heat.resolution: the thermal sensor resolves patches about 100 m across; USGS delivers it resampled to a 30 m grid, and this is on the terrain's 1 arcsec grid
surface_heat.grid: the staged terrain's own 1 arcsec grid, nearest neighbour from Landsat's 30 m
surface_heat.unit: degrees C of the SURFACE, not the air
caveats: A typical-season picture, not a forecast and not today.
Surface temperature, the skin of roofs, roads and leaves. In sun it runs well above air temperature and is not comparable with a forecast figure.
Landsat passes at mid-morning. Afternoon surfaces run hotter and spread further apart.
The thermal sensor sees patches about 100 m across, so this shows a few blocks at best and never a single building or roof.
Water is masked: this is a picture of land.

population_grid.source: GHS-POP R2023A, 2020 epoch, 100 m population count (European Commission JRC), via Earth Engine
population_grid.resolution: 100 m equal-area source, resampled through people per square metre onto a 3 arcsecond (about 93 m) lat/lon grid; a modelled estimate, not a head count
population_grid.unit: people per pixel (a count, not a density)
caveats: A modelled estimate of where people live, at about 100 m. It is not a head count.
Scaled so the staged area adds up to the published figure: the grid says where, the census says how many.

Inside a spot, people are placed on the mapped buildings in their cell, so a spot over open ground holds nobody. Where a cell has people and no mapped building they are spread evenly over the cell instead.
